However, after carefully checking, that ID was never included in their email.

I even attached screenshots of their email and my invoices as proof, yet they still refuse to help. Their support team is unresponsive and unwilling to resolve a simple issue, despite having all the necessary information. To make matters worse, they are delaying the process when I only have 30 days to get my refund.

title: Great app, highly recommend
body:
After using this app daily for seven weeks, I’m very happy with it’s features and functionality. I use it as a personal to-do list and an organizer for my reoccurring tasks. The free version was very good but I decided to upgrade to Pro because I wanted to organize my tasks using more than five projects. I’ve subscribed my projects to my Apple calendar which gives an excellent overview of my tasks combined with my schedule. 

PROS 

- I find their help documentation to be well written and complete. 

- The scheduling functionality (setting, changing, moving, postponing tasks) is well coded and easy to use. 

- I think $5 CAD per month for the Pro version is reasonable. Other apps I’ve researched wanted $12.99 or more per month. I don’t like the subscription model either but that’s where software seems to be going. The key for me is value for money and so far I think $5 per month has been well worth the cost. 

- The developer adds/refines features regularly and often; this is good because the app will remain current and responsive to the needs of the users. 

- The way tasks can be viewed and organized (Today, Upcoming, sections, parent tasks, labels, filters, priority) makes it easy to customize and see exactly what needs to get done. 

CONS 

- The badges are enough for me but I acknowledge many people would see reminders only available in the paid version as a con. 

To sum up, if you want a well-made intuitive app to manage your tasks give Todoist a try.

title: Best App I Own
body:
I’m someone who needs a todo list to function and Todoist has been the centrepiece of my life's organization and scheduling for about 4 years now. 

No complaints. None. It just works exactly the way you want it to.

I work as an office administrator and every single reminder or date goes in as soon as I hear about it. Just type “Meeting fri p1 #work @” and you’ve instantly got a priority 1 task on Friday in your “Work” project. So simple! If your boss says “We should try something different for Christmas next year,” I can set a note to myself that will show up in 11 months, and don’t I look smart for remembering that great idea at the perfect time to implement it. 😎

I’m not an expert at every feature (the shared projects, copying to google calendar, karma), but that means you don’t have to be either in order to get your money’s worth out of this app. I do use the filters quite a bit, and once you read the tutorial, they’re fairly simple to set up. Try a filter for undated todos - things you should schedule but haven’t - and then make a recurring todo to check it every week. Nothing flies under the radar. Or if I’m having a bad day and don’t have a lot of energy, I have a “Essentials” filter for priority 1 tasks in my work-projects - the stress of seeing a 25-item todo list is now only 4 items. I can focus on the important things and chill out.

These are just some of the ways I use Todoist, but it’s super-flexible and doesn’t railroad you into doing things a certain way. Give it a try and find out what works for you!

title: Far more intuitive and capable than Things 3
body:
After a lot of experimenting with both apps - Todoist is far superior in my opinion

The whole organization and implementation of tasks is far more familiar and intuitive

Your ability to add more functionality and depth to your reminders (like voice clips, photos, URL’s, Locations etc…) is immediate and nicely laid out

Trying to even get into those functions in Things 3 is an unnecessary nuisance, or that function is simply missing

Furthermore, once you start getting deeper and fancier into the app, the integrations are far more impressive and useful.

Next, it’s a one-time subscription that works across ALL of your devices from iOS to Windows - very reasonable monthly subscription and you can now use it everywhere (I use a Windows for my desktop and iPad/iPhone for mobile)

Lastly - you can use the free version, get used to it - see if you like it. 

Things 3? - you pay handsomely for each app separately without ever even getting to try it out. No trial period, just pay and find out later. I though by making the purchase that it I would have a trial period, nope! 

There are a lot of people going on about how wonderful Things 3 is, I couldn’t disagree more - Todoist is an all-around better buy - and even the free version is good enough for most people

title: Huge goods & equally impactful bads
body:
I have been using Todoist for a few days and I have mixed feelings. 

On the +plus+ side:
•Natural Language Processing
•advance Date Detection for scheduling
•advance Recurring tasks scheduling
•Attachment capabilities
•Priority indicators
•option to show all attached Labels/Project on tasks without any extra clicking required 
•Reminders for all kinds of things like tasks without due dates, and sub tasks
•advance Reminders like location-based, & multiple reminders for a (sub-)task
•WINDOWS app! Thank you for caring about your cross-platform users.
•Sub-sub tasks!
• “Overdue” indicator in “Today” view
•Sections option in Projects and Child Projects
•Really pleasant Reminders tone that to me feels like a friendly nudge :)
•Fast, smooth & effective syncing between devices
•ability to change, and with many design options for, the App Icon so users can make distinct the Todoist app against a similarly coloured device background/other apps

On the -negative- side:
1) Can’t show a linked Calendar’s events in the app
2) Tasks with attached Priority/Reminder(s) can’t be manually moved up or down the list; i.e. these tasks are automatically moved and fixed to the top of the list. This drives me absolutely mad, especially in the Today view, because I can’t choose to organise the view of my tasks for the day based on my availability/schedule. I don’t want to have to schedule a Due Time for tasks just so  I can place them where I want them on the list. I don’t want to be forced to time everything, and yet Todoist is forcing me to be that kind of to-list user. And I definitely don’t want to have to mark tasks as a Priority if they are not—just so I can move them to the top of the list. Just because I want a visual indicator of tasks’ importance/reminders doesn’t mean I want to be restricted in how I choose to view my tasks for the day. Users should have that flexibility.
3) No “Evening” option in “Today” view 
4) No description once a task is expanded upon being clicked on. To write & view any kind of notes/info, we need to make an additional click to the Comments.
5) UI is functional but not actually aesthetically pleasing, and does not give a “clean” look to mask its complex capabilities. How to do this? Not my area of expertise so I don’t know. I do know it’s possible because it’s been done.
6) Can only view & change the status of “Completed” tasks via the Inbox.
7) Can’t easily delete Sub-Tasks. More clicking required, and can only delete them once at a time. Huge pain if I want to delete multiple sub-tasks at once. That’s a lot of clicking.
8) Big learning curve to use this app, especially the Filters. I just wanted a “Soon” and “Anytime” view which, because they weren’t included in the app, I had to set up via Filters. Took me 12+ hours to learn and get them right. I acknowledge the usefulness of Filters for a variety of more complex needs, but for myself, I haven’t found the hassle and learning curve of setting up Filters quite match up to their daily usefulness.
9) Can’t move tasks out of the Inbox unless they are associated with a Project. I would’ve liked the simplicity of the option of moving tasks out of the Inbox once they are Scheduled.
10) Can’t modify the name or Sub-Tasks of a Recurring task just one time (eg just for Today) without affecting the future occurrence of the task.
11) Can’t Complete a task without all its Sub-tasks be automatically checked off as completed. Why would people want to in the first place? For an accurate future reference of the sub-tasks which were and were not completed, because sometimes you just can’t do them all.

Anyway, that sums up my experience as a new Todoist user. It’s probably simple to deduce I’ve been a Things 3 user, and while Things have limitations as well, for now, I prefer their UX &  UI. I have the Premium Todoist subscription for 1 month, and will use it up with the hope of preferring Todoist over Things...mainly because the plus are huge pluses—and because I spent SO.MUCH.TIME setting up the former.

title: Todoist is on the Right Track
body:
I have always struggled with "to do lists" systems throughout my work and personal life. For every system, I am always gung ho at first and then it seems to fall apart as it gets cumbersome and takes too much time for maintenance of the numerous lists in multiple locations, on paper and different devices.

After a bit of research I found the Todoist, an IOS App.

So far I like it. Would give it an 8-9 out of ten.

What do I like?

1) Very simple entry of items on multiple devices: iPad, iPhone and Web based app
2) Shares well with multiple users. My wife uses it as well. We assign things back and forth to each other. Mostly back! :-)
3) Can organize items into multiple categories which the app call projects. Some of our projects are merely a collections of lists. ie Films to Watch, Places to Visit
4) we have started to use for scheduled events. Both single and repetitive. I think it will replace our calendars but not sure at this time. It does not have a calendar view which is a bit annoying but on the upside the events appear on the appropriate day in One location and are very easily moved if not completed.

We have been using for about three months. It is now the first thing I look at in the morning, which is a good sign.

title: Decent to do app
body:
I apologize this review is a bit lengthy. 

I would say it is decent overall. If you're looking for a basic app that allows you to categorize tasks and assign due dates to them then this will work. One of the biggest advantages to me is that it works on both MacBooks, iPhones and Windows since I use all those platforms in my daily work. I'm only giving it three stars because it does have some features which personally I find a bit lacking.

One of the biggest flaws in my mind is the inability to easily assign a date to a task. The application wants you to spell out a day and time (example typing: tomorrow at 3 PM ) instead of allowing you to choose from a drop-down calendar. I find a drop-down calendar is so much quicker and easier to use.

Secondly, as with most people in their daily routine's, I often have to turn emails into tasks. On the Windows platform this is not so easy to do. You actually have to go to the folder in Windows Todoist application where you want the task to wind up and copy the distinct email address for that folder. Then you have to go back to the email in Outlook and send that email to the Todoist application by pasting the Todoist email address into the recipient box then sending the email to that address. This is rather clumsy and time-consuming. When you're dealing with many emails a day this all adds up.

Lastly, this whole karma thing is a bit annoying. I know you can turn it off, but I would prefer that the developer take their time and effort to improve the application (create more layouts for printing for instance ) rather than spending time on useless information about how much karma you have accumulated from using the app.

Just give me a basic cross platform app that enables me to easily turn emails into tasks and allows me to sort and print task lists in various layouts and I will be happy. Five stars forthcoming.

title: Very good app but...
body:
This is a very very good app. Probably one of the best ToDo type apps out there even better than Appigo's ToDo. But like Appigo, Toodoist lacks direct integration with ICal/Google calendars. There is a workaround using Sunrise calendar which does sync with iCal/Google, but that workaround does not provide 100% integration (it's maybe 90%) and the fact you have to use a "go between" calendar like Sunrise to act as the agent that syncs between Todoist and iCal/Google is not as clean as one might like. Still, the workaround works.

More disappointing, is the developer of Todoist has not provided any indication on when full and direct calendar integration with iCal/Google Calendar will be available. Todoist's on support forum is filled with threads that praise the app but deplore the fact the developer seemingly never responds to this request or even just an update on when calendar integration will be available.

/Dan.

author: Some guy225632

title: Great cross platform app
body:
I have been trying to find an app that can be used both for work and for home. This is my choice. 

Web interface is good, app experience is good. It does not have the same level of complexity as OmniFocus - but we don't all need that. This app offers a balance between simplicity and complexity. 

Feature requests include: better notification time handling and location based reminders.
